headline.title: Chinese tech workers are starting to train their AI doubles–and pushing back
headline.summary: Chinese tech workers are increasingly being asked by employers to train AI agents that could potentially replace them, leading to significant introspection among these early adopters of AI technology. A recent GitHub project called Colleague Skill aims to help users replicate their colleagues' skills and personality traits through AI.

articles.title: NVIDIA and Partners Showcase the Future of AI-Driven Manufacturing at Hannover Messe 2026
articles.summary: At Hannover Messe 2026, NVIDIA and its partners highlighted the transformative impact of AI on manufacturing, emphasizing the industry's shift towards AI-driven production to address challenges such as faster design cycles and labor shortages. The focus is now on the speed and methods of AI adoption in manufacturing processes.

articles.title: Discover and Prove: An Open-source Agentic Framework for Hard Mode Automated Theorem Proving in Lean 4
articles.summary: The article introduces "Discover and Prove," an open-source framework designed for Hard Mode automated theorem proving in Lean 4, which requires systems to independently discover answers before formal proof construction. This framework aims to address limitations in current automated theorem proving benchmarks that often simplify tasks, providing a more realistic challenge akin to human problem-solving.

articles.title: The Illusion of Equivalence: Systematic FP16 Divergence in KV-Cached Autoregressive Inference
articles.summary: A recent study reveals that KV caching in autoregressive transformer inference, commonly believed to be numerically equivalent to cache-free computation, actually leads to divergent results under standard FP16 precision due to non-associative floating-point accumulation. This discrepancy affects the decoded token sequences in multiple open-weight models, including LLaMA-2-7B.

articles.title: (1D) Ordered Tokens Enable Efficient Test-Time Search
articles.summary: A recent study explores the impact of token structures in autoregressive generative models on the efficiency of test-time search. The findings suggest that ordered tokens can enhance the ability to steer generation by allowing for more effective exploration of candidate generations.

articles.title: GTA-2: Benchmarking General Tool Agents from Atomic Tool-Use to Open-Ended Workflows
articles.summary: The article introduces GTA-2, a new hierarchical benchmark designed to evaluate General Tool Agents (GTA) by encompassing both atomic tool use and complex, open-ended workflows. This benchmark aims to better align AI tool-use assessments with real-world productivity requirements, addressing limitations in current evaluation methods.

articles.title: Early Detection of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) Using YOLOv12 Deep Learning Model
articles.summary: A study published on arXiv demonstrates the use of the YOLOv12 deep learning model for the early detection and classification of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) cells, addressing the challenges posed by the visual similarities among different cell types. The research employs two segmentation techniques focused on cell and nucleus features to enhance classification accuracy.

articles.title: Seed1.8 Model Card: Towards Generalized Real-World Agency
articles.summary: The Seed1.8 model is a foundation model designed to enhance generalized real-world agency by enabling multi-turn interactions, tool use, and multi-step execution. It maintains strong performance in language and vision tasks while providing a unified interface for search, code generation, and GUI interaction, along with cost-effective inference options.

articles.title: ARC-AGI-3: A New Challenge for Frontier Agentic Intelligence
articles.summary: ARC-AGI-3 is a new interactive benchmark designed to evaluate agentic intelligence in abstract, turn-based environments, where agents must independently explore, infer goals, and plan actions without explicit instructions. This benchmark continues the focus of its predecessors on assessing fluid adaptive efficiency in novel tasks, while avoiding reliance on language and external knowledge.

articles.title: 1S-DAug: One-Shot Data Augmentation for Robust Few-Shot Generalization
articles.summary: The article presents 1S-DAug, a novel one-shot generative augmentation method designed to enhance few-shot learning by creating diverse variants from a single example image at test time. This approach combines traditional geometric perturbations with controlled noise injection to improve model generalization to novel classes.

articles.title: Security Threat Modeling for Emerging AI-Agent Protocols: A Comparative Analysis of MCP, A2A, Agora, and ANP
articles.summary: The article conducts a comparative analysis of emerging AI-agent communication protocols—Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A), Agora, and Agent Network Protocol (ANP)—highlighting their roles in facilitating multi-agent interaction and interoperability. It emphasizes the need for standardized threat modeling to address the security principles that are currently underexplored in these protocols.

articles.title: The 12-month window
articles.summary: Many AI startups are emerging in areas not yet covered by existing foundation models, but this opportunity is expected to diminish over time. Industry experts suggest that the current 12-month window for innovation in these categories may soon close as foundational models expand.
